title: Webull - General discussion
body:
O.P.
Their KYC is super invasive, is it like this everywhere now ? Sending copies of linked back accounts seems fraught with issues, when they are inevitably hacked?
Cash Transfers So I transferred some money in from my Macquarie, it's in the Moneybull account (seems to indicate there's an auto sweep that puts cash management money there anyway ?)
https://www.webull.com.au/he lp/faq/1590-What-is-Moneybull
We will start to sweep your uninvested AUD cash to the AUD Money Market Fund on the next business day.
So, how do I transfer funds out if it's in the Moneybull account ? you cant transfer out of Moneybull directly to an external bank account ? I assume you need to go to your Webull cash management account (how ?) but if you do that its swept back in to the Moneybull account (or that's how I read the above ?)

---- replies ----
[User #5094038659 postsThe One-Armed ManWithout chemicals, he pointsWhirlpool Forums Addict] There is a "Redeem" button at the bottom of the Moneybull section of the app. Once that is done, in t+2 your redemption amount will be available for exchange or withdrawal.

The One-Armed Man writes...
There is a "Redeem" button at the bottom of the Moneybull section of the app
I assumed though, because it does say the Moneybull is set up to sweep from the cash management account (does it?) that when i transfer out of Moneybull to the cash management account, it will sweep back in to Moneybull ?
(see down the bottom Step 2 (Auto sweeps uninvested cash to money market funds) https://www.webull.com.au/moneybull
I even emailed them on how as my cash management section has a 62c balance and the rest of the cash is in my moneybull and I wanted to test a withdrawal to my Bank Account to understand how it all worked, there reply was
Thanks for reaching out to us. I am happy to assist.
There no limit on the daily transfers out
Maybe you can set a retained amount on the Moneybull page,
that doesn't seem to be an answer as to how to withdraw and I am not sure I even know what that means:).
to be fair going in I conflated Moneybull with my Webull Cash management account and it was only when I started poking around I found it wasn't.
Now that I am using it for AUD Monybull (AUD) is kind of redundant, I can transfer cash in seconds form my own Cash Management Account that pays higher interest
[User #5094038659 postsThe One-Armed ManWithout chemicals, he pointsWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
Kenjataimu writes...
I can transfer cash in seconds form my own Cash Management Account that pays higher interest
If we're just talking about AUD then Moneybull doesn't serve a great purpose IMO, because, as you say, you can transfer from your external HISA bank account and trade.
Money that is redeemed from Moneybull isn't re-swept back into it, as far as I'm aware. I did a small redemption a few days ago to test, and it's sitting there as Available to Withdraw (or Exchange).
If you have Moneybull AUD and you want to trade US stocks, it's a bit cumbersome because you have to redeem, wait a day or two, then convert. Not the way I wanna go about things.
Their customer support (phone) is pretty good, you should call them to clarify and confirm the above. I'm not holding myself out as an expert. As a rule, I generally don't hold funds in a brokerage account.
[User #5094038659 postsThe One-Armed ManWithout chemicals, he pointsWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
More generally, there are several things to like about Webull. I've had an account with them since they started here.
CHESS sponsored broker (ASX)
Brokerage-free trading in ETFs (AUS, US)
Interest is paid on uninvested funds (Moneyball)
App UI is polished and snappy
Customer service has been good (phone support, no long waits, Australia-based)
Generous promotions/referral bonuses in the past, although this seems to be winding down a bit.
They're never going to be my all-in-one broker, but you can pick and choose what you use them for.

[User #92684918 postsAtjoyI'm new here, please be nice] You can hold AUD Moneybull and trade ASX. In your case, you need to redeem first, and then convert to USD.
I think the whole point of Moneybull is that it lets you trade with Moneybull account balance and earn a return on your sales proceeds. If you are looking for higher interest, but not trading, bank accounts still offer a better rate if your cash balance is under 250K.
